1. A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃. What is the 
speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height? 
A. 𝑣0. 
B. 𝒗𝟎𝐜𝐨𝐬𝜽. 
C. 𝑣0sin𝜃. 
D. 0.
questions.stem:
A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃. What is the 
speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?

options.explanation: At maximum height, only the horizontal component of velocity remains, not the initial speed.
The horizontal component of the velocity remains constant throughout the projectile motion.
The vertical component of the velocity is zero at maximum height.
The speed is not zero because the horizontal component is still present.

questions.source_raw:
2. A spaceship is traveling with an initial velocity of 𝑣⃗0=(20.1 𝑚/𝑠)𝑖̂ when its rockets 
fire, imparting an acceleration of 𝑎⃗=(2.02𝑚𝑠2⁄)𝑖̂+(4.03𝑚𝑠2⁄)𝑗̂. Based on this 
scenario, which of the following statements is correct? 
A. The x-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant . 
B. The y-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant . 
C. Both the direction of motion and speed change . 
D. None of the above is correct.
questions.stem:
A spaceship is traveling with an initial velocity of 𝑣⃗0=(20.1 𝑚/𝑠)𝑖̂ when its rockets 
fire, imparting an acceleration of 𝑎⃗=(2.02𝑚𝑠2⁄)𝑖̂+(4.03𝑚𝑠2⁄)𝑗̂. Based on this 
scenario, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The x-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant.
options.explanation: The x-component changes due to the x-component of the acceleration.

options.text: The y-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant.
options.explanation: The y-component changes due to the y-component of the acceleration.

options.text: Both the direction of motion and speed change.
options.explanation: Acceleration in both x and y directions change the speed and direction of motion.

options.text: None of the above is correct.
options.explanation: There is a change in both speed and direction, making option C correct.
